name: Claude Canvas
tagline: Prebuilt Ink TUI canvases Claude Code spawns in tmux panes

license.notes: MIT. README: 'This is a proof of concept and is unsupported.'

adoption.summary: 1.5k stars and 138 forks gathered in its launch week (Jan 2026, shared widely on X/LinkedIn), then no further commits. No known production users; no releases.

maintainability.release_cadence: No GitHub releases; 19 commits total, all between 2026-01-06 and 2026-01-08
maintainability.bus_factor: low: dormant single-author proof of concept
maintainability.summary: A launch-week demo that was never maintained after; treat as an idea, not a dependency.

architecture.summary: A Claude Code plugin (marketplace + skills) plus a Bun CLI. `canvas spawn <kind> --scenario <name> --config '<json>'` opens a prebuilt Ink/React canvas (calendar, document, flight) in a tmux split pane. The canvas and the controller talk over a Unix domain socket: canvas to controller sends ready/selected/cancelled/error; controller to canvas sends update(config)/close/ping. A TypeScript high-level API (pickMeetingTime, editDocument, bookFlight) spawns a canvas and awaits the user's selection.
key_points: Fixed catalogue of hand-written canvases; the agent picks kind + scenario and supplies JSON config
IPC over a Unix socket with a tiny message vocabulary (update/close/ping; ready/selected/cancelled/error)
Delivered as Claude Code skills that teach the model the CLI
Mouse support inside canvases; tmux is required

tui-canvas (Czaruno, 0 stars, MIT, Jan 2026) ports the idea to an MCP server with a protocol-first design and OpenTUI/Ink implementations; jredville/tui-canvas (0 stars) is a Go persistent markdown canvas with a socket daemon

agent_usability.how: Claude Code skills instruct the agent to run the Bun CLI (spawn/show) with JSON config; the controller can send `update` with a new config over the socket. tui-canvas wraps the same idea as an MCP server.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Install the plugin (/plugin marketplace add dvdsgl/claude-canvas); needs Bun and a tmux session. New canvas kinds require writing Ink components.
agent_usability.readback: Only the user's result comes back (selected/cancelled events with data). The agent cannot read the rendered screen or canvas state.
agent_usability.granular_edits: No; `update` replaces the canvas config wholesale.
agent_usability.summary: A pleasant demo of 'give the agent a second screen', but the agent is limited to choosing among prebuilt canvases and receiving a selection.

score_notes.ui_as_data: only the config is JSON; each canvas is hand-written Ink code
score_notes.agent_drivable: CLI + socket protocol for spawn/update/close of prebuilt canvases
score_notes.readback: selection events only, no screen or state read
score_notes.live_data_rate: ad hoc config pushes; no data sources
score_notes.maturity: self-described unsupported proof of concept, dormant since Jan 2026

steelman: claude-canvas proved the demand in one week: 1.5k stars for the simple idea that a coding agent deserves its own display next to the chat, in the terminal, with real interaction (pick a meeting slot, select text to edit, choose a seat) rather than more scrolling text. Its design is pleasingly small: a skill, a CLI, a tmux split and a six-message socket protocol, with a typed async API that turns a canvas into a function call that returns the human's choice. That 'canvas as an awaitable question to the human' pattern is exactly what agents need for approvals and choices, and it works in any tmux today with no new terminal or framework.
weaknesses: Self-described unsupported proof of concept; no commits since 2026-01-08
Fixed set of three canvases; new UIs require writing React/Ink code
No readback of the screen or state; agent only receives the final selection
tui-canvas forks have zero stars and little activity

relation_to_scene.overlap: An agent opens a terminal UI beside the conversation and exchanges messages with it over a Unix socket.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Nothing substantial; scene already exceeds it. The awaitable 'ask the human and wait for selected/cancelled' round trip is the one thing done cleanly here.
borrow: An awaitable high-level call (e.g. scene.ask(ui) -> {selected, data} | {cancelled}) for approvals and pickers
Ship the agent integration as a Claude Code plugin/skill with a marketplace entry
Spawn into a tmux/herdr split automatically when available
relation_to_scene.gap_left: claude-canvas has no UI-as-data, no readback, no patches, no data streams, no history, no pixels; thc-scene does all of these.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: A dormant demo whose one good idea (awaitable human choice) is easy to borrow; it is not a foundation.
